provenance.title: Generalised geological / geomorphological belts of the North Eastern Region
provenance.description: Six generalised belts used to give the hazard engine a rock-mass credibility term. Boundaries follow published regional geological maps (GSI / ONGC syntheses) at a coarse level of detail: they are axis-aligned envelopes of the belt extents, not surveyed polygons.
provenance.accuracy: Belt assignment is indicative to roughly 10-25 km. `erodibility` is an expert-assigned relative index (0-1) for landslide-prone material behaviour under monsoon rainfall, not a geotechnical parameter.
references: GSI, Geology and Mineral Resources of the North Eastern Region (Misc. Publ.)
Nandy, D.R. (2001) Geodynamics of Northeastern India and the adjoining region

erodibility_note: Weights reflect known landslide behaviour: Neogene molasse and ophiolite/melange belts fail most readily; stable granitic and plateau basalt terrain fails least. Values are relative within this region.

belts.name: Higher / Tethyan Himalaya
belts.note: High-grade metamorphics and Tethyan sediments, glacially over-steepened; rock-avalanche and debris-flow dominated.

belts.name: Lesser Himalaya
belts.note: Low-grade phyllite, schist and quartzite with deep weathered profiles; the classic monsoon landslide belt.

belts.name: Siwalik / Sub-Himalayan foothills
belts.note: Weakly cemented Neogene sandstone-conglomerate; among the highest recorded shallow-landslide densities in India.

belts.name: Shillong Plateau (Garo-Khasi-Jaintia)
belts.note: Archaean gneiss and intrusive granite capped by laterite; failure is controlled by jointing and the plateau edge scarp.

belts.name: Indo-Burma fold belt (Naga-Chin-Arakan, Barail, Tripura-Mizoram)
belts.note: Turbiditic flysch (Barail, Surma, Tipam) with ophiolite melange; rapid tectonic uplift and very high relative relief.

belts.name: Brahmaputra / Barak alluvial plains
belts.note: Recent alluvium of the valley floors. Flood and bank-erosion dominated; slope-driven landsliding is rare except at terrace edges.

precedence_note: Overlapping envelopes are resolved in the listed order, so the narrow valley floors are not absorbed by the broader fold-belt envelope.
